title: Vendor names on the command line: Claude is refused, claude works
lead: *Proposed.* `--implementer Claude:sonnet:high` (and `--reviewer`, `--architect`, `ork vendor out Claude`) is refused as an unsupported vendor, while `claude:sonnet:high` works, and the error does not list the valid names. This slice makes vendor names case-insensitive and stored lowercase, and makes an unknown name's error list the vendors, in the CLI and in the daemon (owner answers 2026-11-04). The accepted list is derived from `supportsVendor`, so it includes the `-local` vendors once S301a adds them.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-04: ork wave start ... --implementer Claude:sonnet:high is refused as unsupported vendor; claude:sonnet:high works. The daemon matches vendors exactly (runner.go:90, runs.go:471-474) while matrix rows are matched case-insensitively (runs.go:428).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** model and effort spelling (passed to the vendor CLIs as given; not checked here); aliases such as the matrix's `Claude Code` on the command line (Q3); new vendors.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner evidence, 2026-11-04: `ork wave start ... --implementer Claude:sonnet:high` was rejected with "unsupported vendor", and the lowercase spelling worked.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-04; anchors re-checked 2026-11-07 at a1114e2):

- `lineupFlags.apply` (`internal/cli/lineup.go:36-77`) splits `VENDOR:MODEL:EFFORT` at the first and last colon (`:59-67`) and keeps the vendor as typed. The CLI does not check it.
- The daemon checks it: planRun returns `bad params: unsupported vendor %q for %s` when supportsVendor fails (`internal/daemon/runs.go:471-474`). `supportsVendor` is an exact match on `claude`, `codex` or `grok` (`internal/daemon/runner.go:90`). The error does not list them. `TestRunPlanRefusesBadOverride` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go:398`) has the case "unsupported vendor" with `acme`.
- `ork vendor out|back NAME` matches exactly against `vendorNames` (`internal/cli/vendor.go:16`, `:76-78`). Its error does list them: "unsupported vendor %q; use claude, codex or grok". The daemon's vendor.set handler also lists them (`internal/daemon/vendors.go:60`).
- The matrix path is already case-insensitive: `matrixAdapters[strings.ToLower(row.Agent)]` (`matrixAdapters` at `internal/daemon/runs.go:349`, used at `:429` and `:448`; `internal/daemon/matrix.go:76`; `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:115`), where a matrix agent `Claude Code` maps to `claude`. So the plan shows lineups taken from rows named `Claude Code`, while the flag needs `claude`.
- The engine and runners compare vendors exactly (`internal/daemon/runner.go:29`, `:92-100`; `internal/engine/brief.go:100`; `internal/engine/round.go:52`). So a non-normalised name must not reach them; normalising at the edge (CLI and wire) is enough.
- The vendor list is about to grow. S301a (S301, open, handled elsewhere) adds `claude-local`, `codex-local` and `grok-local` to `supportsVendor` (adj 188). Today the three names are written out in four places: `supportsVendor` (`runner.go:90`), `vendorNames` (`internal/cli/vendor.go:16`), the vendor.set error (`internal/daemon/vendors.go:60`) and the CLI error built from `vendorNames` (`vendor.go:20-21`). So this slice derives the accepted list and every error text from the one list behind `supportsVendor`, and hard-codes no names.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/lineup.go:59-67` (normalise or check the vendor of each entry).
- `internal/cli/vendor.go:16` and `:76-78` (`vendor out|back`).
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:471-474` (normalise the wire's lineup entries before `supportsVendor`, and list the vendors in the error) and `internal/daemon/runner.go:90` (`supportsVendor` reads the one exported list).
- `internal/daemon/vendors.go:60` (`vendor.set`).
- `internal/cli/run_test.go` (beside `TestRunLineupFlagUsageErrors` at `:614` and `TestLineupErrorsNameCommandAndFlags` at `:635`), `TestWaveStartLineupFlagsApplyToEveryItem` (`internal/cli/wave_test.go:447`), `TestVendorCommandUsageErrors` (`internal/cli/vendor_test.go:100`), `internal/daemon/runs_test.go:398`.
- `docs/guide.md:200-205` (the lineup flags) and `docs/design.md:1317` (CLI).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
The owner chose Q1 option 3 (both), Q2 cli-and-daemon and Q3 no (2026-11-04), so every test below applies except the one marked option 2 only, which is dropped.

Normalising (Q1 option 3):

- `TestLineupVendorIsCaseInsensitive` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): for `run p S1` and `wave start p S1 S2`, each of `Claude:sonnet:high`, `CLAUDE:sonnet:high`, `Codex:gpt-5:high` and `GROK:latest:high` in `--implementer`, `--reviewer` and `--architect` sends the lineup with vendor `claude`, `codex` or `grok` (lowercase) to `run.plan` and `run.start`; model and effort are sent as typed. Fails first: the vendor is sent as typed.
- `TestRunPlanNormalisesVendorCase` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`): a `run.plan` wire lineup with vendor `Claude` plans with `claude`. Fails first: "unsupported vendor \"Claude\"".
- `TestVendorOutIsCaseInsensitive` (`internal/cli/vendor_test.go`): `ork vendor out Claude` sends `claude`. Fails first: "unsupported vendor \"Claude\"".

Listing the vendors (Q1 option 3). The expected list in each test is built from the exported list (`daemon.Vendors()` or its final name), never typed out, so S301a's three `-local` names need no test change:

- `TestUnknownLineupVendorListsTheVendors` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): `--implementer acme:m:high` exits 2 with "ork: run: --implementer: unsupported vendor \"acme\"; use " plus the list, before any daemon call. Fails first: the daemon's error, without the list.
- `TestRunPlanUnsupportedVendorListsTheVendors` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`): the `acme` case of `TestRunPlanRefusesBadOverride` says "use " plus the list. Fails first: no list.
- `TestVendorNamesHaveOneSource` (`internal/daemon`): `supportsVendor(v)` is true exactly for the names in the exported list, and the vendor.set error text holds each name. Fails first: no exported list.
- (Dropped: `TestMixedCaseVendorSuggestsLowercase` was for Q1 option 2, which the owner did not pick.)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. One place for the names: export the list from `internal/daemon` (for example `daemon.Vendors()`), and make `supportsVendor` a lookup in it. The accepted list is whatever that list holds: today `claude`, `codex` and `grok`; after S301a also `claude-local`, `codex-local` and `grok-local`. *Proposed* reading of Q3 ("only claude, codex and grok"): it means the vendor names `supportsVendor` accepts, not matrix agent names such as `Claude Code`; the owner may correct this. Build every error list (`vendor.set`, `planRun`, the CLI) from it. Drop the CLI's second copy, `vendorNames` (`internal/cli/vendor.go:16-21`). Whichever of this slice and S301a lands second adds its names to, or reads from, the one list.
3. Q1 option 3 (decided): `strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(v))` on the vendor in `lineupFlags.apply`, in `vendor out|back`, and on every lineup entry of the `run.plan` / `run.start` wire in `planRun` before the check. The engine and run record see only lowercase names.
4. Q1 option 3 (decided), Q2 cli-and-daemon (decided): the CLI checks the vendor in `apply` and fails with the listed vendors (`vendorList()`, built from the exported list). The daemon error lists them too.
5. Update `docs/guide.md` (the lineup flags: vendor names are case-insensitive; an unknown name gets the list) in the same diff.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/cli ./internal/daemon -run 'Vendor|Lineup|BadOverride'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- Mutation: remove the lowercase step in `planRun`; `TestRunPlanNormalisesVendorCase` goes red.
- [HUMAN CHECK] `ork run P ID --implementer Claude:sonnet:high` shows a plan whose implementer row reads `claude`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Vendor names are case-insensitive; errors list the vendors".

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body:
UI slice by rule u10 (`internal/cli` output), so it gets a UI pass.

All three questions were answered on 2026-11-04 (owner, interactive; see the note): Q1 both (accept any case and store lowercase; an unknown name gets the list of vendors). Q2 cli-and-daemon. Q3 no (only vendor names, no matrix agent names such as `Claude Code`). Since S301a adds `-local` vendors, the accepted list is the one `supportsVendor` uses (Implement step 2); no new question.
